title: Underwriting Rule: One Larkspur Valuables Floater per Customer
content:
**Underwriting rule.** A customer carries one Larkspur Valuables Floater, and all of that customer's items are scheduled on it: the maximum is 1 floater per customer. A floater is bound only when the customer holds no other valuables floater that is bound or in force, and the customer's primary residence is insured on a live Larkspur HomeGuard, CondoGuard or RentGuard policy.

## What the rule is judged on

- **Evidence.** Both parts of the condition are read from the company's records for that customer before the floater is bound: the customer's existing valuables floaters and their status, and the customer's residence policy. What the caller says about other floaters does not replace the records.
- **Object.** The check is made for the customer the new floater would be bound to; floaters held by any other customer are not counted.
- **Both parts.** The condition has two parts and both must hold.

## Judgement table

| The customer's records show | Other floater part | Residence part | Floater may be bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| No other valuables floater; primary residence on a live HomeGuard policy | met | met | yes |
| Another valuables floater with status bound | not met | met | no |
| Another valuables floater with status in force | not met | met | no |
| Only an earlier valuables floater that is cancelled or expired; primary residence on a live RentGuard policy | met | met | yes |
| No other valuables floater; primary residence not insured on a live HomeGuard, CondoGuard or RentGuard policy | met | not met | no |

## Basis Q&A

**The customer wants a second schedule for items kept at another address. Is a second floater written?** No. All items are scheduled on the customer's one floater; a second floater that would sit alongside a bound or in-force one is not bound.

**The customer's earlier floater expired last year. Does it stand in the way?** No. Only a floater that is bound or in force counts against the rule.
